correctness.rationale: A word with no disjoint repeated length-n factor induces a walk in the order-(n-1) de Bruijn graph. The source proves that each factor w can occur at most ceil(n/per(w)) times. Walk edge multiplicities therefore obey these capacities and have incidence 0 or e_s-e_t, proving the general relaxation bound. For k=2,n=7, two independently formulated optimizations agreed on a minimum deletion of 16 from total capacity 236. The final package replaces numerical optimization by exact integer certificates: dual potentials prove deletion cost at least 16 for all 4033 endpoint choices, and one feasible deletion vector has cost 16. Thus the relaxed walk maximum is exactly 220 and C(2,7)<=226.

value.rationale: The source explicitly identifies improvement of its C(k,n) upper bound as an open direction, and C(2,7) is the first unresolved binary parameter after exact values through n=6. The new global compatibility constraint reduces the published 242 upper bound to 226, cutting the gap above the published lower bound 192 from 50 to 34, a 32% reduction. The de Bruijn-flow formulation is also reusable for other k,n rather than being an arbitrary one-off enumeration.
